patch_description: The current algorithm already vectorizes the LPT greedy across layers, but its packing quality (especially expert-level balancedness, 0.25) is limited by plain cardinality-constrained LPT, which is only a 4/3-approximation and leaves local imbalance. My key insight: after the greedy assignment, most residual imbalance is pairwise — the heaviest pack contains small items that could trade places with large items in the lightest pack. I add a vectorized-across-packs, per-layer local-search refinement that repeatedly swaps the smallest-weight item in the most-loaded pack with the largest-weight item in the least-loaded pack whenever the swap strictly reduces the spread. Swapping preserves both the cardinality constraint and rank-in-pack uniqueness (the two items simply exchange packs and inherit each other's slots). Since `balanced_packing` is used both for node packing (Step 1) and GPU packing (Step 3), the refinement improves balance at every level of the hierarchy while adding only a few cheap CPU tensor ops per round. The replication step is unchanged (its greedy weight/logcnt split is already near-optimal for a divisible-load model), keeping execution time near the current 0.01s while improving both GPU and expert balancedness scores.
